sharp_stability_source_issue.source_inference: The remainder after extracting Fourier coefficient at xi has e^{-i xi x}; absolute integral is then bounded using the unmodulated H^{1/2} remainder and signed H^{-1/2} potential-difference norm.
sharp_stability_source_issue.why_invalid: Negative Sobolev duality bounds the signed pairing against the modulated remainder, not the integral of its absolute integrand. Multiplication by e^{-i xi x} costs up to <xi>^{1/2} on H^{1/2}.
sharp_stability_source_issue.explicit_general_counterexample: For nonzero real chi in C_c^infty(B_r), let Q_N=chi cos(Nx1), v=chi, xi=N e1. Then ||Q_N||H^{-1/2}=O(N^{-1/2}) but integral Q_N e^{-iNx1}v tends to (1/2)integral chi^2>0. Proof: two translated Schwartz Fourier profiles give the norm bound by splitting at |eta±Ne1|=N/2; oscillatory integral term decays by integration by parts. This refutes the uniform modulated-duality inference, not the full restricted CGO conclusion.
